chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Home life, practicing and the records he bought
summary: He painted the house, practiced on an upright Steinway, and bought records for sound: Bird, Mahalia Jackson, Paul Robeson, Hawkins, Tatum and Ellington.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: One of the things I was curious about, in talking about the domestic scene, is interests that you had outside of music and things that you would do when you weren't working, given that you worked at the Paradise...
Well I used to...I painted the house and fixed up the lawn and do little things around the house and buy things for the house, you
know what I mean, and it was, you know, a real domestic scene. And I'd practice. I had an upright Steinway and I had records and I was content, you know.
Did you buy a lot of records at any time? I mean was that a thing that you...

No, that wasn't a thing. There was things that interested me, you know, 'cause when Bird came out with his things I bought some of his records and Norman Granz. I listened to them. And then I began to hear Mahalia Jackson. I bought some of her things because of the sound, you see. I'm very sound conscious. And Paul Robeson, I bought some of his things, because of his sound. And Coleman. I didn't have all of one thing. If a person had a sound, it didn't matter if they were a singer or a musician, if I liked the sound. Of course Tatum and then Duke's band. I liked that sound, the overall sound and that's the kind of records I bought, yeah.
